Is respiratory illness rising in this ne.answer: I can't tell you that about a neighborhood, and neither can any public dataset we have. Respiratory emergency-visit data covers the whole four-county Health Service Area (Fulton, DeKalb, Clayton and Gwinnett), not a tract. Flu and COVID numbers are only reported for the whole Clayton, DeKalb, Fulton, Gwinnett area, not for your neighborhood. The latest numbers we have are from 2024-09-28. The plan gives it no weight.

Who does this plan reach?.answer: The four catchments reach about 261,169 of 1,051,550 residents. Flagged for human review: Hispanic or Latino: catchments reach 4.5% vs 7.2% county-wide (parity 0.63 < 0.80). Asian: catchments reach 3.8% vs 7.3% county-wide (parity 0.52 < 0.80). Limited English: catchments reach 1.1% vs 1.7% county-wide (parity 0.65 < 0.80). This comparison is auditor-only: the planner never saw race or ethnicity.
